detail: Found by a field teammate reading the store directly, then reproduced locally against the real GraphStore. graph-auto-populator.ts:53,68 stamps file/directory entities with properties:{scope: input.scope}. GraphStore.addEntity (graph-store.ts:59-65) upserts by merging {...existing.properties, ...input.properties}, so the incoming scope OVERWRITES the stored one. Reproduction: addEntity('docs/project-map.md', file, {scope:'analysis/'}) then addEntity(same name/type, {scope:'specs/cui-marking/'}) -> same entity id, properties {"scope":"specs/cui-marking/"}, original scope unrecoverable. Field evidence matches exactly: analysis/project-map.md moved analysis/ -> specs/cui-marking/; CLAUDE.md .claude/ -> analysis/cmmc/; specs/POC-READINESS-RUBRIC.md specs/hitl-plane/ -> analysis/cmmc/; two templates analysis/ -> analysis/cmmc/. Two consequences: (1) any scope-filtered graph query returns wrong membership for files touched from multiple scopes — precisely the shared/cross-cutting files most worth graphing; (2) every re-scope rewrites the entity JSON, producing recurring git churn in .twining/records/graph/entities/ that reads as meaningful change but is not. NOT FIXED — the right semantics are a design call (accumulate a scope set, first-writer-wins, or drop scope from file entities entirely) and belong to the owner, not a review pass. This class was missed by the 59 because it only appears when graph-auto-populator and graph-store are composed.
summary: NEW confirmed bug (not in the 59): graph entity scope is last-writer-wins — a file touched by decisions in two scopes loses its original scope irrecoverably
